newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen falling after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen falling after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening lower on Friday following strong February nonfarm payrolls data, analysts said.

"This is very strong data, way above expectations and bonds are down sharply. It's tellings us that there is a possibility the Fed may raise rates at the next meeting on March 25," Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities.
"Looking at the bonds and the futures I'd have to say we will have a bad day."
However, some analysts did not share Zagorski's gloom about the jobs data which showed February nonfarm payrolls jumped 339,000, compared to a rise of 247,000 in January.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected a gain of 230,000, but some analysts saw market-friendly details in the jobs report.

Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said: "The news is okay. It's certainly not going to move the Fed to move rates, simply because of the fact the hourly workweek was up 0.3 percent and that is good news. It shows a very modest increase."
